sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Foreign Market Feasibility Study and Regulatory Licensing Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national-level LLC jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction; Suez Canal Economic Zone remains administratively separate but within the same national legal order)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law of Napoleonic lineage with commercial statutes of French inspiration, Islamic Sharia serving as the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Constitution of 2014
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United States Treaty Concerning the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (in force 1986)
Egypt–China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1994, amended by Protocol in 2016)
Egypt–United Kingdom Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1975)
Egypt–Netherlands Agreement on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1996)
EU–Egypt Association Agreement (2004), including investment-related disciplines
Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA) and Agadir Agreement (2004)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 194 of 2020, together with the Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 12 of 2021 (as amended), which mandate beneficial-owner identification, customer due diligence, record-keeping and reporting to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU); Law No. 94 of 2015 on Combating Terrorism and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 1067 of 2015); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Ministerial Decree No. 342 of 1982 issuing its Executive Regulations, which require LLCs to maintain an updated internal register of shareholders and beneficial owners; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI one-stop-shop incorporation rules; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976 for registration formalities.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: the LLC must maintain an internal beneficial-ownership register; shareholder details are filed with the Egyptian Commercial Registry and GAFI and are accessible to EMLCU, the Financial Regulatory Authority, GAFI, tax authorities and the judiciary upon lawful request, but the beneficial-ownership layer is not searchable by the general public; nominee arrangements must still reveal the ultimate natural person to the competent authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, commercial register extract or equivalent trade licence of the foreign corporate shareholder (or identity and address proof for an individual foreign shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry or competent commercial authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so the document must be authenticated by the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate, followed by sworn Arabic translation before delivery to the Egyptian notary/GAFI

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the foreign corporate shareholder, together with the board resolution or shareholders' resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and the appointment of its manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary, corporate secretary or competent registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization in the absence of Egypt's accession to the Apostille Convention; certified Arabic translation required; the Egyptian Notary Public (Mu'aqqibat) shall authenticate the Arabic incorporation contract

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney granted to the Egyptian incorporation agent, covering signature of the memorandum/statutes, filings with GAFI and the Commercial Registry, and opening of the corporate bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Consulate in the shareholder's country of origin, or home-country notary followed by Egyptian consular legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization and sworn Arabic translation; the notarized original must be physically deposited in the GAFI/Commercial Registry file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter, source-of-funds evidence, and passport copies of each beneficial owner and proposed manager, with notarized translation as necessary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country regulated bank and passport-issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for corporate bank references; passport copies may be certified by the Egyptian Consulate or a sworn translator; all documents become part of the AML/CDD file retained by the Egyptian corporate-services provider

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every shareholder, manager, signatory and ultimate beneficial owner against (i) the EMLCU national designation and freezing lists, (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, including resolutions 1267/1989 and 2253 regarding ISIL and Al-Qaida, (iii) the OFAC SDN List and other OFAC sanctions programs, (iv) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and (v) domestic PEP designations as defined in Law No. 80 of 2002 and EMLCU implementing guidance. Standard CDD must be completed before execution of the incorporation documents; enhanced due diligence is triggered on any PEP, sanctions, adverse-media or politically exposed connection. Screening results, copies of identification and underlying transaction documents must be retained for no fewer than five years after the end of the business relationship, in accordance with the Executive Regulations of the AML law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Egyptian Commercial Registry electronic services portal Tachira (https://www.tachira.gov.eg/) and the GAFI Investor Services one-stop-shop portal Invest in Egypt (https://www.investinegypt.gov.eg/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LLC name must be expressed in Arabic script and must carry the mandatory legal-form suffix 'ذ.م.م' (sharikat that mas'uliyya mahduda / LLC) or an officially approved Latin transliteration where foreign shareholders require a bilingual name. The Commercial Registry rejects names that are identical or deceptively similar, on a phonetic and literal basis, to existing registered names or well-known trademarks, taking into account Arabic transliteration of foreign names; names implying Egyptian state, religious or financial authority are disallowed without prior ministerial consent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Credit, Financial, Investment, Securities, Brokerage (require prior licensing or no-objection from the Central Bank of Egypt or the Financial Regulatory Authority)
Insurance, Re-Insurance, Takaful (require prior authorization from the Financial Regulatory Authority)
Islamic, Sharia, Al-Azhar, Religious (require prior consent of the competent religious authority)
Ministry, Ministerial, Government, State, Public Authority, National (in an official capacity context, require cabinet or competent ministry approval)
Governorate, Municipality, Police, Military, Intelligence, Suez Canal Authority (require the specific authority's prior written approval)
Arab Republic of Egypt, Egypt (when used as a state denomination or with official connotation), and the names of sovereign national symbols or the President
Blasphemous, obscene, or inciting terms rejected outright by the Commercial Registry discretion
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Commercial Registry/GAFI rejects a proposed name, the applicant shall obtain the written reasoned refusal and may (i) file a corrected fresh application under a revised name, at nominal re-filing cost and without loss of priority, or (ii) submit a written grievance in Arabic to the GAFI Investor Support Unit or the Commercial Registry Complaints Division within 15 working days of the refusal. If the grievance is denied or remains unanswered for 30 days, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the State Council (administrative judiciary) after exhausting the administrative remedies, and may concurrently reserve an amended name to preserve the filing date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the statutory head office: an Egyptian LLC must maintain a physical registered head office (al-maqarr) within the governorate of incorporation, evidenced by a valid lease contract and a clearly visible Arabic signboard; a virtual or serviced office may be used only as an auxiliary correspondence address and must never be filed as the registered address for service in the Commercial Registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 10–15% probability of an unannounced GAFI or Commercial Registry inspection within the first 12 months for a standard low-risk management consultancy LLC classified under ISIC 7020; inspection risk increases if the registered address is a mail-drop, the Arabic signboard is absent, or the authorized manager is not reachable at the registered office, in which case the registry may strike off or suspend the registration for false head-office declaration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and Commercial Registry Tachira pre-screening reservation fee (one-time application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory service tariff, EGP-denominated nominal fee per name reservation application, converted at prevailing market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the Arabic memorandum and articles of association, incorporation file, board resolution of the foreign shareholder, and ancillary corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Egyptian legal counsel / corporate-services firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a single-member LLC with one foreign corporate shareholder, fixed-fee engagement of approximately USD 800–1,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication of the incorporation contract before the Egyptian Notary Public (including e-notary and digital-signature option if used) and Ministry of Justice stamp and service fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Authority, Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff applied to LLC incorporation documents, EGP-denominated stamp and service fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of foreign corporate documents by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate and sworn Arabic translation of the four-document authentication bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Embassy/Consulate abroad and sworn translator registered with the Egyptian Chamber of Translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular statutory fees per document plus prevailing market rate of approximately USD 30–60 per translated document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register setup, EMLCU-compliant CDD file preparation, and PEP/OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening of shareholders, managers and beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance advisor / Egyptian corporate-services provider, including screening software licence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard CDD/EDD screening and beneficial-ownership register preparation, one-time engagement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI one-stop-shop incorporation processing fee and Commercial Registry registration fee for a standard LLC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Egyptian Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariffs prescribed under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, EGP-denominated

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic publication of the incorporation notice in the Commercial Registry bulletin / official gazette electronic channel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff, fixed nominal amount under the current e-registry practice, replacing legacy newspaper advertisement fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint Stock Companies, Partnerships with Limited Shares, and Limited Liability Companies, as amended, together with its Executive Regulations; Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment, where applicable. LLC formation and governance matters are governed primarily by Articles 20-34 (formation) and Articles 39-46 (management) of Law No. 159/1981.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department / One-Stop-Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Etaa Wal Nizaam) registered with GAFI and the Commercial Registry, resulting in the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration Extract
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on limited liability companies under Law No. 159/1981. The founders freely determine the capital amount. The subscribed capital must be fully paid, deposited in an authorized Egyptian bank in cash or valued in-kind, and certified by the bank before registration. No separate escrow account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding members unanimously adopt the Articles of Association of the Limited Liability Company and authorize the incorporation filing with GAFI. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each founder subscribes to the shares stated in the shareholding schedule, that the subscribed capital is treated as fully paid into the company's designated Egyptian bank account, and that the registered office at the address specified in the Articles is adopted as the statutory seat of the company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the founder appointed as General Manager is hereby authorized to execute all registration filings, open banking accounts, engage legal advisors, and take every necessary action to obtain licenses, permits, and tax registration for the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Form Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the GAFI electronic portal with three proposed Arabic names. The registry checks for identical or confusingly similar existing registrations and confirms that the LLC form is available for the proposed activity.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport copies of all founding members
Power of Attorney if a corporate shareholder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected, submit a revised name list within five business days; no additional penalty is imposed and the review is automatically repeated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office (Shahr Al-Tawqee') or GAFI-designated notarization counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic (English translation may be attached), sign all founding members in person or through authorized attorneys, and have the signature and legal capacity of each member notarized before the competent notary official.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Valid national ID or passport of each founding member
Power of Attorney for each authorized signatory
Registered office lease agreement or title deed copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a notarial objection due to signature mismatch or missing attestation, correct the affixing of signatures and resubmit the instrument to the same notary office; the process is typically cured within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Temporary Bank Account and Capital Deposit Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company bank account in the name of the proposed LLC using the notarized Articles of Association and the founders' identification. Deposit the subscribed paid-up capital in the account and obtain a bank certificate confirming the capital deposit for presentation to GAFI.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Passport copies and tax identification numbers of founders
Name reservation confirmation
Bank account application and forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the deposit certificate because of discrepancies in names or share values, amend the capital schedule and Articles with the founders' unanimous consent, pre-notarize the amendment, and reapply to the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Association together with the bank capital certificate and lease documentation through the GAFI online or physical counter. GAFI reviews the file, assigns the company enterprise number, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Commercial Registration Extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Lease agreement or property authorization for the registered office
Passport copies of founders and authorized officers
Name reservation certificate
Form of founders' declarations and address attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a procedural query based on incomplete documentation, the applicant has fourteen days to provide the missing documents or execute the requested amendments. Re-filing through the One-Stop-Shop is permitted without loss of the original application priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Authority Registration and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and the National Organization for Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, Commercial Registration Extract, lease agreement, and officer ID documents to the ETA to obtain the tax identification card and applicable tax file. Register the company with the social insurance authority for employee enrollment, and if annual taxable supplies exceed the threshold, complete VAT registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Registration Extract
Valid ID and passport copies of directors
Registered office lease agreement
Bank account details
Employee status declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed because of incomplete officer records, submit a formal correction letter together with the missing identification documents and obtain the tax number retroactively; social insurance enrollment may be filed separately without blocking tax registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority applies; General Authority for Industrial Development has no jurisdiction over ISIC 7020 management consultancy activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license required for ISIC 7020. A local administrative office occupancy notification and Civil Defense safety clearance may be required for the physical office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA report or environmental registration is required for non-industrial consultancy and office-based business activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to office consultancy operations. Business must comply with general municipal wastewater discharge norms and waste disposal regulations of the Cairo/Giza Governorate if office-generated waste is handled outside designated municipal collection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Civil Defense Authority is required for the office premises and must be obtained after physical inspection of fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, and electrical load safety. A workplace occupancy clearance may also be issued by the district administrative authority after confirming structural load safety and compliance with basic occupational health requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt; electronic portal: www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned LLC must file a tax registration application with the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) prior to commencing commercial activity. Required steps: (1) obtain Commercial Registration extract and Chamber of Commerce certificate; (2) execute a notarized power of attorney appointing the LLC's managerial representative in Egypt; (3) submit certified articles of association, lease/purchase agreement for the registered office, and valid owners'/managers' national IDs (or passport copies for foreign managers); (4) open a corporate bank account in Egypt and obtain a bank certificate; (5) file ETA Form 1 ('Tax Card') application with supporting dossiers; (6) upon inspection and approval, ETA issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and a Tax Card evidencing VAT, payroll, and corporate income tax registration statuses.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Egyptian LLC is subject to corporate income tax under Law No. 91 of 2005; no pass-through status is available to LLCs)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Egypt does not operate a check-the-box regime and does not recognize fiscal transparent LLCs for income tax purposes. No hybrid mismatch or consolidated/unitary tax elections are available; the LLC is mandatorily taxed as a separate juridical entity on worldwide income, and foreign shareholders are taxed on distributions solely at the shareholder level at the relevant non-resident dividend rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, with executive regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for resident/established suppliers; non-resident service suppliers have no de minimis threshold and must register for VAT in Egypt from the first taxable supply if the place of supply is Egypt and no reverse-charge mechanism applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing applies to VAT-registered businesses under ETA's real-time clearance mandate (introduced progressively from 2020). Registered suppliers must issue invoices in ETA-compliant XML/JSON format via the integrated e-invoicing API, obtain a QR-digital stamp from the ETA clearance server before dispatch, and submit all e-invoice transactions to the ETA for approval. Taxpayers must maintain an API credential (digital signature certificate) and can be blocked from clearance without valid authorization.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods and services are zero-rated under Article 4 of the Egyptian VAT Law if the following cumulative conditions are satisfied for consultancy services: (a) the recipient is a non-resident person; (b) the service is wholly performed, economically utilized, and consumed outside Egypt; (c) the consideration is in convertible foreign currency and actually transferred to, and repatriated through, an Egyptian bank account; (d) contracts, service reports, and invoices demonstrate an overseas engagement; and (e) the supplier is VAT-registered and has filed the relevant export service list with the ETA. For goods, the exporter must produce a valid customs export declaration and prove the goods physically left Egypt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (fully accepted electronic ACD/AED)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank FX transfer receipt
Service export contract and service report (for ISIC 7020 consultancy)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA may disallow the zero rate and retroactively claw back input VAT claimed as refundable, with late-payment interest (currently applied per the VAT law) and an additional punitive fine of up to 100% of the tax evaded for negligence or false documentation. Fraudulent use of forged customs or FX instruments triggers the general tax evasion penalties under Law 67/2016, including monetary penalties up to EGP 100,000 and imprisonment for individuals, and a denial of the foreign supplier's or exporter's refund rights. ETA also cross-checks export invoices with customs declaration data and Central Bank FX records; any discrepancy can trigger indirect red-flag audits and export eligibility suspension.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) acting through its Banking Supervision Sector and Foreign Exchange Control Department, pursuant to the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE foreign exchange circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with current account liberalization for goods, services, and unilateral transfers, but retains capital account restrictions and CBE approval/notification requirements for certain cross-border transactions. Profit and dividend remittances by foreign-owned Egyptian LLCs are permitted through licensed banks upon presentation of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and CBE-verified corporate documentation; however, FX liquidity in Egyptian pounds can cause practical conversion and settlement delays, particularly during balance-of-payments stress, so material profit repatriation should be planned after confirmed FX availability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE regulations, export proceeds must be fully repatriated to an Egyptian bank account within 75 days from the date of shipment or completion of the service. The mandatory surrender ratio is effectively 100% for export receipts: all proceeds must be credited to a bank account in Egypt in convertible foreign currency, with the exporter permitted either to retain the foreign currency in an FX account or to sell it to the bank at the prevailing interbank rate for Egyptian pounds. Supporting documents include the export invoice, bill of lading/airway bill or service delivery certificate, copy of the customs declaration, and the bank credit advice.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Egypt does not permit unlicensed offshore fintech EMIs or digital banks to operate domestic EGP clearing, maintain local-currency corporate accounts, or act as official channels for CBE reporting and export-proceeds surrender. Wise B2B may be used only as a supplementary outward-payment facilitation layer for non-EGP corridors after the mandatory Egyptian bank rail has been used for capital inflow, FX conversion, and statutory reporting; it cannot replace a licensed Egyptian corporate bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is strongly mandated for the first corporate KYC interview. In practice, at least one authorized signatory or legal representative must attend a bank branch in Egypt with original passport, corporate register extract, notarized board resolution, and apostilled powers of attorney for foreign shareholders/directors. Remote/video interviews are accepted by certain banks only as a supplementary step after a local attorney-in-fact or nominee officer completes physical KYC; full remote opening without any Egypt-based representative is generally not accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque beneficial ownership structure involving foreign shareholders or layered intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, consolidated memorandum and articles, full shareholders register, signed UBO declaration for every natural person holding 25% or more, notarized board resolutions, a clear group organizational chart, certified copies of passports of ultimate beneficial owners, and apostilled powers of attorney for each nominee and signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch between the amount of proposed capital injection and the parent entity's income profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of parent bank statements, audited consolidated financial statements, tax clearance certificates from the parent jurisdiction, invoices or underwriting agreements explaining accumulated profits, board resolution approving the injection, and a detailed written explanation of source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list hit, weak adverse-media screening, or politically exposed person (PEP) finding on any shareholder, director, or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full sanctions screening reports from reputable databases, beneficial owner and management declarations, adverse-media narrative with official court/registry records, PEP status explanations including public-office evidence and source-of-wealth documents, and, if applicable, an independent legal opinion confirming no exposure to UN, EU, OFAC, or CBE sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial-purpose ambiguity for a cross-border market-entry consultancy receiving foreign-currency payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed feasibility-study engagement letter, detailed scope-of-work describing overseas market entry consulting and regulatory license agency services, target market entry plan, evidence of office or agent relationship in Egypt, projected cash-flow schedule of foreign client receipts, and the corresponding CBE transaction purpose code declarations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital from the overseas parent must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to a licensed Egyptian beneficiary bank, using the CBE-prescribed inward remittance purpose code for foreign direct investment or capital subscription. The LLC's Egyptian bank must hold the corporate KYC file, the CBE capital and banking transaction registration, evidence of the parent's board approval, and proof of the underlying shareholder agreement; the bank will credit the capital account in foreign currency or convert to Egyptian pounds at the interbank market rate after verifying the source of funds and completing CBE reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound service fees, trade settlements, and operating payments should be executed through SWIFT MT103 payment orders or MT202 cover payments, with commercial letter of credit (LC) settlements handled via MT700/MT710 (issued/amended documentary credit) and MT600 series settlement messages where applicable. Each payment instruction must include the correct CBE outflow purpose code, the underlying invoice or contract, a tax clearance certificate or withholding-tax receipt if the service is subject to Egyptian withholding tax, and, when payable in foreign currency, the bank's FX conversion record evidencing the applicable interbank rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Egyptian pound deliverable FX forwards with a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank, covering genuine commercial or financial underlying exposure of the LLC
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the Egyptian pound transacted with an international bank or through a licensed Egyptian bank, using USD/EUR net settlement to hedge convertibility risk
Cross-currency swaps (fixed or floating) executed under an ISDA master agreement with a counterparty that holds a valid Egyptian financial license or complies with CBE counterparty-capacity rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ETA Form 15) with Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Corporate Income Tax Assessment Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the tax year-end; 30 April for calendar-year LLCs (the default tax year is the Gregorian calendar year unless ETA approves an alternative fiscal year at formation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment addition of 2% per month on unpaid tax; fine up to EGP 100,000 for failure to file; ex officio assessment on a 3-year lookback basis; criminal referral for evasion carries fines of EGP 20,000-100,000 and possible imprisonment of the responsible manager

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) Register Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and the Egyptian Money-Laundering and Terrorist-Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March confirming UBO data as of 31 December; any share-transfer or ownership change must be updated within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EGP 500,000 for false or omitted UBO disclosure under AML Law No. 80/2002 (as amended by Law No. 172/2020); EMLCU may block bank accounts and file criminal charges against the responsible manager for serious breaches

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Egyptian Tax Card (Taxpayer Registration Card) Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Taxpayer Registration Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, filed by 31 January to validate the tax card for the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An expired tax card blocks tenders, bank-business transactions, customs clearance, and commercial registry endorsements; ETA may impose an administrative fine of up to EGP 10,000 for operating without a valid card

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Authority / General Authority for Government Services (GAFS), Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every 5 years on the registration anniversary; renewal application may be lodged no earlier than 6 months before the expiry date and must be completed before the registration lapses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EGP 10,000 plus monthly surcharges for late renewal; prolonged lapse results in administrative strike-off, suspending the legal capacity to invoice, contract, or maintain bank accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Social Insurance Wage Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Authority for Social Insurance (NASI) - Employers' Registration and Collections Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage schedule and payroll register filed with the January monthly contribution return (due by 31 January); final annual reconciliation due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 2% on unpaid contributions; deliberate under-declaration of wages attracts fines of EGP 500-10,000 and retroactive assessment of up to 5 years of insurable earnings under Social Insurance Law No. 148/2019

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax Reconciliation Statement (WHT Form 41)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Withholding Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly WHT remittances and statements are due by the 15th of the following month; the annual reconciliation and certificate of amounts withheld are due with the corporate income tax return by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly 2% addition on unremitted withheld tax; responsible manager is personally liable for withheld amounts; deliberate failure to withhold carries a fine equal to the unreported tax and criminal referral under Law No. 91/2005

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified audit is compulsory under the Executive Regulations of Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 when gross annual turnover exceeds EGP 1,000,000 (approx. USD 20,000-25,000); GAFI additionally requires audited statements for LLCs with non-resident quota holders or paid-in capital above EGP 250,000; ETA may compel an audit in any selected-case review even below these thresholds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), mandatory under the tax law and fully converged with IFRS; foreign parent groups may maintain parallel IFRS books for consolidation; statutory books must be kept in Arabic, with bilingual Arabic/English being the market standard for foreign-owned consultancy LLCs

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Cabinet Decree No. 2675/2021 and AML Law No. 80/2002, the LLC's manager must keep an updated UBO register at the registered office and report any quota transfer to the Commercial Registry/GAFI within 30 days; where no change occurs, an annual UBO confirmation signed by the manager covering the December 31 position must be lodged with GAFI (for LLCs with non-resident quota holders) or retained in the statutory register file by 31 March; non-resident shareholders failing annual identity recertification may have their dividend and loan accounts suspended by the AML compliance officer
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Partners' and Managers' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,200 per year (Cairo registered-office address and registered-agent statutory mail handling via licensed corporate-services provider)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 500 - 2,500 per year (mid-market Egyptian audit firm for a consulting SME; Big-4 range approximately USD 4,000 - 8,000)
